doc.title: Delfeayo Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sideman years: Fats, Ibrahim, Blakey, Elvin
title: Kenny Garrett and how the Elvin invitation came
summary: Kenny Garrett was musical director with Blakey but said little; Marsalis contrasts this with being called up by Elvin.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Who was the musical director for Blakey’s band while you were there?
Kenny Garrett. Kenny Garrett was there.
Did he talk to you? Or did he give you any guidance?
He didn’t really talk much, no, no.
But you’re all about the same age – generation.

It was a strange – Kenny was at the tail end of the other band. The situation was not really that hip, actually. Like I said, the way that I came into that particular band was – it wasn’t as natural – you know what I mean? – as when I played with Elvin. But playing with Elvin, I sat in at a gig with Elvin, and he was like – he called me up, said, “Come join the band.” I said, “Whoa, okay.”
